host_memory_note: free -h at run start: 15Gi total, ~13Gi free. Peak measured RSS across all four target subprocesses: 2.02 GB (INV-1), 1.86 GB (INV-7 p_fail), 4.44 GB (INV-8), 6.64 GB (INV-7 p_exist, killed at wall-clock cap while still climbing) -- all well under the 11 GB internal / 13 GB external soft/hard memory caps; no memory-cap termination occurred in this run (all four terminations/completions were either clean level-boundary completion or the external wall-clock cap, never the memory cap).
packages_used: python3 standard library only (fractions, hashlib, itertools, math, subprocess, signal, json, time, os, datetime)
background_process_management: Each target enumeration ran as its own subprocess.Popen, launched sequentially (never concurrently), monitored by an external parent process polling /proc/<pid>/status VmRSS every 2.0 seconds (see memory-timeseries-<target>.json for each target's full continuous sample series) and enforcing a hard external wall-clock cap of 6000.0s (kill via SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after a 3s grace period) plus a hard external memory cap of 13.0 GB, independent of the worker's own internal soft caps (11.0 GB memory / 5700.0s wall clock, checked only between completed complexity levels). CRITICALLY, unlike the prior repair run, EVERY completed complexity level is ALSO checkpointed continuously to a separate on-disk file (checkpoint-<target>.json, atomic write-then-fsync-then-rename) by the worker itself -- independent of and in addition to the external monitor's own memory-timeseries log -- so a hard kill (real, tested by an actual SIGKILL delivered mid-run to a live worker process before any target-related run in this task; see stdout.log / this run's execution-report notes) preserves every completed level's result durably.
one_disclosed_deviation: A stray subprocess from an ABORTED alternate invocation attempt of the p_exist-only driver (killed by the executor within seconds of noticing the invocation mistake, per this run's stdout.log) briefly re-ran and OVERWROTE checkpoint-INV-1_mean.json twice with an incomplete in-progress state before being killed; both times it was regenerated verbatim from the untouched, already-complete worker-result-INV-1_mean.json (written by the original, uninterrupted INV-1 run and never itself touched by the stray process). Disclosed in full in implementation.md and the execution report; the final checkpoint-INV-1_mean.json and worker-result-INV-1_mean.json on disk both reflect ONLY the original, real, uninterrupted enumeration run.
